q: A club president exposed the 1971 Bundesliga match-fixing scandal by playing secret tapes at his fiftieth birthday party. Which club?
sub: Fifty-two players were punished and Arminia Bielefeld lost its licence.

q: Borussia Mönchengladbach won 12-0 on the last day of 1977-78 and still lost the title. Which club took it on goal difference?
sub: Köln won 5-0 at St Pauli the same afternoon.

q: Which club's fans celebrated a Bundesliga title for four minutes in 2001 before Bayern Munich equalised in stoppage time at Hamburg?
sub: German newspapers called them the champions of hearts.

q: Which club won the 1967-68 Bundesliga and was relegated the very next season?
sub: Max Merkel had torn up the title-winning side, thinking it too old.

q: Which club was left out when the Bundesliga was founded in 1963 and had to wait until 1965 to get in?
sub: Only one Munich club was allowed, and 1860 Munich had won the Oberliga.

q: Which German club beat Inter Milan 7-1 in 1971 only for the result to be wiped out after a fan threw a can at Roberto Boninsegna?
sub: The replay in Berlin finished 0-0 and Inter went through.

q: Which second division club beat Borussia Mönchengladbach on penalties to win the 1992 German cup?
sub: No club from outside the top flight had ever managed it before.

q: Which club's reserve side lost the 1993 DFB-Pokal final to Bayer Leverkusen, the only time a second string has got that far?
sub: Ulf Kirsten scored the only goal of the final.

q: Which Bayer Leverkusen striker was given a goal at Hoffenheim in 2013 after his header went wide and through a hole in the netting?
sub: The 2-1 result stood and Hoffenheim's appeal was thrown out.

q: Which German referee was jailed in 2005 for fixing matches, among them a cup tie in which Paderborn beat Hamburger SV 4-2?
sub: He was also banned from football for life.

q: A Bayer Leverkusen goalkeeper scored a penalty at Schalke 04 in 2004 and was lobbed from the halfway line while celebrating. Who?
sub: Mike Hanke scored straight from the kick-off.

q: Which club filled its own pitch with around 800 sofas brought from home so that fans could watch the 2014 World Cup together?
sub: They called it the World Cup living room.

q: German fans threw tennis balls and chocolate coins onto pitches and locked bike locks to goalposts in 2024. What did they stop?
a: The sale of a stake in the league's media rights to a private investor
sub: The DFL dropped the deal in February 2024.

q: Which club dropped to the amateur fourth tier in 2017 when its Jordanian investor refused to pay for a third division licence?
sub: Hasan Ismaik wanted control that would have broken the fifty plus one rule.

q: Which club went down from the Bundesliga in 1995, was then refused a second division licence over its debts, and fell to the third tier?
sub: They spent more than a decade in regional football.
